paper.title_en: A Zoology of Quantum Turing Patterns
paper.abstract_en: We explore quantum Turing pattern zoology, where the same Lindblad equation supports a morphology atlas of stripes, spots, holes, labyrinths, and defects. The stable stripe species provides a quantitatively controlled case in which morphology and Gaussian witness loss separate parametrically. In particular, visible Turing stripes can remain after two Gaussian witness margins associated with the same $k_*$ mode cross zero in a completely positive Lindblad lattice. The witness thresholds on the exact shell fall as $\mathcal{N}^{-1}$. The stripe nematic threshold tends to a nonzero value at fixed lattice size, time window, and morphology criterion. The ratio of the morphology threshold to either witness threshold therefore grows with $\mathcal{N}$. Imaging and momentum-resolved covariance measurements probe these sectors separately.
